On the traces and quick triage: attaching a short diagnostic summary in the bridge notes (p95-traces-20270725.zip). Top findings so far:
- The compact-int8 variant reduces memory footprint but triggers an unoptimized kernel path for long-context requests (>1024 tokens) on our older Ampere nodes. That path currently falls back to a CPU-bound decoder for specific attention patterns, which explains the p95 inflation and throughput drop.
- We observed increased KV cache invalidation around the model swap (likely because the variant id differs) causing repeated recompute for long sessions.
- A small subset (~2.6%) of requests hit a quant-decode mismatch that produced malformed token sequences (these correspond to the hallucination samples).

Immediate recommended actions (order matters):
1) Rollback Kestrel namespace to v3.1-fp16 immediately (this reverts kernel selection).
2) Disable compact-int8 routing for customers on older Ampere hardware until we patch the kernel path.
3) Short-term: increase concurrency cap for Kestrel to absorb backlog (already queued).
4) Medium-term: patch kernel selection to avoid CPU fallback and add an automated KV-preservation step during variant swaps.

ETA for rollback (with ops): 20–30 minutes once we get approval. I will start the runbook if Marissa gives the sign-off.

Irene Choi
Senior SW Engineer, Runtime & Serving | Redwood Inference
